source_text: Nos igitur verum diximus, quoniam qui a vobis decipiuntur, ne vocentur haeretici, fiunt Manichaei et, dum falsam verentur infamiam, verum crimen incurrunt instar ferarum, quae circumdantur pinnis, ut cogantur in retia et in verum exitium vana formidine contrudantur. Deum vero nascentium conditorem ita dicimus, ut quoniam certum est Deum catholicorum, qui verus est, nihil facere posse, quod malum est, ipsius opificis dignitate homines, qui ab eo fiunt, ante voluntatis usum de manibus eius iniqui et rei nullo modo exire credantur; quorum vos cum alterum negatis, utrumque subruitis. Ais quippe credere te quidem conditorem Deum, sed malorum hominum, ac per hoc infitiaris dogmati tuo, cum negas te asserere diabolum hominum conditorem.
pass_a_gloss: We therefore have said true, since those who are deceived by you, lest they be called heretics, become Manichaeans and, while they fear a false infamy, they incur a true crime like wild beasts which are surrounded by feathers that they may be forced into nets and by vain fear be thrust into true destruction. But we say God the founder of those being born thus, that since it is certain that the God of catholics, who is true, can do nothing which is evil, by the dignity of the workman himself humans who are made by him are believed by no means to go out from his hands unjust and defendants before the use of will; of which when you deny the other you undermine both. For you say you believe indeed God the founder, but of evil humans, and through this you deny to your dogma, when you deny that you assert the devil the founder of humans.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: We therefore spoke truly: those deceived by you become Manichaeans to avoid being called heretics. Fearing a false disgrace, they incur a real crime, like wild animals surrounded by a line of feathers to drive them into nets, forced into actual destruction by an empty fear.

We call God the creator of newborn children in this sense: since it is certain that the God of catholics, who is the true God, can do nothing evil, the dignity of the maker himself forbids belief that the human beings he makes come from his hands unjust and guilty before they use their will. By denying one of these points you undermine both. You say you believe God is the creator, but the creator of evil human beings. Consequently you contradict your own doctrine when you deny asserting that the devil creates humans.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
